intro: The detector knows 8 whale species. Seven of them are listed here; for each: what it sounds like, whether it is heard at the Monterey Bay hydrophone, and its US protection status. Unchecked claims are marked as such.

species.name: Blue whale
species.sound: Very low pulses and moans, about 15–40 Hz, below what most people can hear. MBARI tracks its 'B call' at 42–43 Hz.
species.monterey: Song heard July through February (MBARI, 2015–2021). Calling follows krill-rich upwelling and shifts from night to day in autumn as migration begins.

species.name: Fin whale
species.sound: '20-Hz pulses': short downsweeps from about 40 to 13 Hz, repeated for hours.

species.name: Humpback whale
species.sound: Long, changing songs of tonal and pulsed units; feeding calls around 500 Hz.
species.monterey: Song heard August through June, on every recording day in November. Days with song rose from 34% to 76% between 2015 and 2021 (MBARI).
species.status: Endangered (Central America population) and Threatened (Mexico population), US ESA

species.name: Killer whale (orca)
species.sound: Clicks for echolocation, whistles, and pulsed calls. Each Pacific Northwest pod has its own learned set of calls, like a family dialect.
species.monterey: Recorded at the Monterey hydrophone at times; which population and how often is not verified. Orcasound's hydrophones in the Salish Sea focus on the Southern Residents: 76 whales on 1 July 2026 (J pod 27, K pod 15, L pod 34).

species.name: Minke whale
species.sound: The North Pacific 'boing': a short pulse near 1.3 kHz followed by a 2.5-second tone near 1.4 kHz.
species.monterey: Presence at the Monterey hydrophone not verified.
species.status: Not ESA-listed; protected under the Marine Mammal Protection Act

species.name: Bryde's whale
species.sound: Pulses and moans, mostly below 60 Hz; in the North Pacific also the metallic 'biotwang'.
species.monterey: A warm-water species (about 40°S to 40°N), so Monterey Bay is near the edge of its range. Presence at the hydrophone not verified.

species.name: Right whales
species.sound: A 2-second 'upcall' rising from about 50 to 440 Hz, and loud 'gunshot' sounds.
species.monterey: The North Atlantic right whale (about 384 left at the start of 2024) never reaches the Pacific, so any 'Eg' detection here is a false alarm. The North Pacific right whale's eastern population is under 50 animals and very rarely seen off California.

known: MBARI's hydrophone sits on Smooth Ridge, about 30 km offshore at roughly 900 m depth, and has recorded almost continuously since July 2015.
MBARI already publishes detectors for blue whale calls, fin whale calls, humpback song and shipping noise, and used them on six years of data (Ryan et al. 2025).

Google trained the detector partly on recordings from this same hydrophone. Finding something new means looking for what these detectors are not built to count: rare species, odd hours, unusual sounds.
